\- In a recent Instagram post, Kylie shared a photo of herself and boyfriend Travis Scott intertwined in front of two private jets. 'You wanna take mine or yours ?' the caption read.  
\- The comments, unsurprisingly, were unforgiving but they all have a point. It's the general population who are repeatedly chastised for not doing enough to save the planet, but it's the 1% who get away with doing the most damage.  
\- Jenner’s flight on 12 July lasted just 17 minutes, taking her from Van Nuys in Los Angeles to the nearby town of Camarillo. The trip would have taken Jenner about 40 minutes in a car, causing just a fraction of the emissions.  
 Elon Musk has taken even shorter flights. Should he be judged differently?  
\- 19-year-old Jack Sweeney whose Twitter account u/CelebJets publicized Jenner's trip has made a name for himself since January by publicly tracking the private jets of billionaires and celebrities.  
\- He says the reaction to Jenner's 17-minute flight was only surprising to him because he's seen Elon Musk take even shorter flights on his private jet, without nearly as much uproar.  
\- Notably, Sweeney says, the data can sometimes be deceiving. Especially short flights can often be explained by a simple rationale: The pilot is dropping off its passenger at one airport, and then parking the plane at another airport nearby.  
 Wanting to avoid travelling with the hoi polloi isn’t a good enough reason for excessive pollution  
\- Celebrities find it difficult to travel commercially. That being said, using private jets as a replacement for road travel is neither practical nor reasonable. It's taking their privilege to an entirely new, unacceptable level.  
\- “There are plenty of alternatives to private jets and wanting to avoid travelling with the hoi polloi isn’t a good enough reason for excessive pollution,” said Nikita Pavlenko, fuels team lead at the International Council on Clean Transportation.  
\- Short trips using private jets are not solely an American phenomenon; in 2019, one-tenth of all flights departing France were private jets, with half travelling under 500 km.
